Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-05-26T00:48Z, as well by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2026-05-25T20:53Z to 2026-05-26T01:23Z. The source of this event is likely continued far sided outflow following earlier CME: 2026-05-25T22:12Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-05-26T02:12Z, as well by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is likely continued far sided outflow following earlier CME: 2026-05-25T22:12Z and field line movement along the NW limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, STEREO A COR2. There isn't a clear source, but there are moving/opening field lines visible in the SE as seen in SDO/AIA 193 around 2026-05-26T04:40Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-05-26T05:36Z, as well by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is likely far sided field line movement seen in SDO AIA 193 and continued outflow following earlier CME: 2026-05-25T22:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint, narrow CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-05-26T06:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO 3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is likely continued far sided outflow following earlier CME: 2026-05-25T22:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Bright streamer blowout CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME appears to be visibly wider in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 than in STEREO A COR2 imagery, which is likely due to the separate perspectives.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement using width of CME from STEREO A COR2's perspective. This measurement may be updated with later frames in SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 only. This is likely far-sided, but no direct source is observed in available low-cadence STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only plane-of-sky as the only observing coronagraph, and lack of observed source (likely far-sided from Earth). STEREO A currently at W58.8, putting its west plane-of-sky at W148.8 for this analysis.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in only a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2 before fading into background. The source is likely far-sided from Earth, and may be observed as slow field line movement beyond STEREO A's SW limb (limb ~W148.8 with STEREO A at W58.8) in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting as early as 2026-05-26T13:05Z and lasting several hours, past the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky as the only observing coronagraph, and likely but unclear far-sided source visible only as slow field line movement beyond STEREO A's SW limb. No STEREO A COR2 visibility of the front. Front fades into the running difference background after several frames.

data.note: CME observed to the NE only in SOHO LASCO C2, fading after a few frames. The source is on/just beyond the NE limb as filament ejecta and field line movement in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-05-26T20:05Z. A second filament ejecta follows immediately after directed further northward, responsible for separate overlapping CME: 2026-05-26T21:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis, using E90 as the observed source longitude approximation and not as a plane-of-sky.

data.note: CME observed to the NE only in SOHO LASCO C2, fading after a few frames. The source is on/just beyond the NE limb as filament ejecta and field line movement in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-05-26T21:09Z. This CME immediately follows and overlaps with CME: 2026-05-26T21:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis, using E90 as the observed source longitude approximation and not as a plane-of-sky.

data.note: Very faint partial halo CME observed in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, also in LASCO C3 obscured heavily by the pylon (and difficult to observe outside running difference imagery in all). STEREO A COR2 in a data gap at this time. The source may be some field line movement and breaking loops observed around 2026-05-26T21:39Z to the SE only in GOES SUVI 284, tracing to an approximate source on-disk around S30E53 (and could vary slightly, due to the brightness of this cluster of regions in SUVI 284).

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 tracking using the approximate source ~E53 and using the partial halo shape for the width. Due to the faintness of this front and no COR2A to triangulate, the latitude, longitude, and width could vary.

data.note: This event is visible to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery following a data gap between 2026-05-26T20:23Z to 2026-05-27T01:23Z. Due to the data gap, it is possible that the start time for this event is earlier than what is listed. This event is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 or in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery due to a real-time data gap between downlink periods. The source for this event is unknown and may therefore be far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 148 degrees as the source may be far-sided and a source location is therefore unknown.

data.note: This event is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an eruption centered near N17E90 starting around 2026-05-27T02:00Z which exhibits northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location. As this event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery and a triangulated measurement is not possible, the measured parameters may vary slightly.

data.note: Faint SE partial halo CME in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and visible to the SE in STEREO A COR2 at 2026-05-28T01:38Z. The source of this event is likely very faint dimming and field line movement seen centered at approx. S20E20 as seen in SDO AIA 193, starting as early as around 2026-05-27T19:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Front is much more wide in STEREO A COR2 than SOHO and GOES, and that is used for the width while tracking the LE in all coronagraphs.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in STEREO A COR2, and S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, difficult to resolve in early frames but becoming more defined as it travels into the field-of-view. This front may be related to a slow, faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-05-28T01:57Z centered around S33E28 south of AR 14436 (S16E29). Though early, that source could also relate to later CME/streamer blowout 2026-05-28T09:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E in STEREO A COR2, and extremely faint in LASCO C2 only resolvable in running difference imagery. The source may be faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-05-28T05:04Z centered around S38E18 south of AR 14436 (S16E27).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between good visibility in STEREO A COR2 and poor visibility in SOHO LASCO C2, but still able to track a related leading edge between both for several frames.

data.note: Faint event observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 only, likely due to the faint feature. No direct source for this event is observed, and is likely far-sided from STEREO A as well as Earth.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only plane-of-sky taken at W149, with the spacecraft currently at W59.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Source is likely a far-sided filament eruption observed on/near the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 starting around 2026-05-28T06:15Z, also observed on/near the SW limb in GOES SUVI 284/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME visible well to the E in STEREO A COR, and as a faint partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 comprised of multiple overlapping features, clearly a complex structure. This front may be related to a slow, faint dimming in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-05-28T01:57Z centered around S33E28 south of AR 14436 (S16E29), which is more directly attributed to earlier CME: 2026-05-28T03:38Z but this front at T9:23Z resembles more of streamer blowout and could simply be outflow following from that first signature. No distinct eruptive activity is seen relating to this start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 with good confidence in fit and leading edge, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 with less confidence due to the leading edge being difficult to follow and appearing much less wide than COR2. The COR2 perspective is used for the width.

data.note: Faint event observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 only, likely due to the faint feature. No direct source for this event is observed, and is likely far-sided from STEREO A as well as Earth.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only plane-of-sky taken at W149, with the spacecraft currently at W59.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-05-28T19:53Z, and this event is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an eruption near Active Region 14455 (N18E63) starting around 2026-05-28T19:30Z which exhibits northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/195/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, the measured parameters may vary slightly.
